correctness.rationale: For a generic Gaussian normal G, the section meets the relative interior of each of the two i-facets exactly when |G_i| is less than the sum of the other absolute coordinates. These transverse intersections give all section facets without duplication; inactive equalities and nongeneric ridge degeneracies have Haar measure zero. At most one strict dominance is possible. Independently, for m=d−1 use absolute coordinate ratios x_i=|G_i|/|G_0| on the solid simplex sum x_i<1. The z^m Jacobian for z=|G_0| gives the normalization c^m E|G_0|^m/m!=1/[π^(m/2)Γ(m/2+1)] by duplication. Under the unweighted normalized product measure the ratios are the first m coordinates of Dirichlet(1,...,1) with one slack coordinate, and z² is χ²_(m+1), independently. Thus the remaining factor is E exp(−X), X=(z²/2) sum x_i². A symbolic calculation via multinomial index partitions reproduced all four moments about 1; the first two are −2/(m+2) and (3m+8)/[(m+2)(m+4)], with the third and fourth O(m^−2). Since X−1≥−1, the cubic Taylor remainder is bounded by e|X−1|^4/24, giving the claimed 7/(2m) and error order; multiplying by d and applying Stirling gives the displayed equivalent.
